articles.author: TV News
articles.description:
TL;DR:

At Washington State Summer Con, Cobra Kai villain Martin Kove allegedly grabbed and bit costar Alicia Hannah-Kim’s arm when she stopped to say hello, leaving visible bruises and nearly drawing blood. Kove told police he was just “messing around” like they do on set, apologized afterward, and was promptly escorted out—Hannah-Kim filed a report for the record but opted not to press charges.
Why it matters:

Kove’s character John Kreese is infamous for his nastiness in The Karate Kid universe, and this off-screen bite certainly lived up to that reputation—though the real-life fallout seems to have ended with bruised egos rather than court dates.
articles.title: 'Cobra Kai' villain Martin Kove kicked out of fan event after he allegedly bit costar Alicia Hannah-Kim.

articles.author: TV News
articles.description:
The Boys Season 5 Wraps Filming

Judging by Jensen Ackles’s comments and a wrap-party post from Isabella Crovetti (and brother Cameron) dated June 21, 2025, Prime Video’s flagship superhero satire has officially wrapped shooting on its fifth—and final—season. While cameras are down, expect plenty of post-production magic, so don’t pencil in a September premiere just yet.
Kripke’s Finale Fears

Showrunner Eric Kripke admits he’s “in a fair amount of terror” about sticking the landing—especially knowing how many series fizzle at the end. On Sony’s Creator to Creator podcast, he and Shawn Ryan broke down lessons from Breaking Bad’s Vince Gilligan, emphasizing the payoff of long-baked story threads and nailing those final emotional moments.
articles.title: ‘The Boys' Final Season Wraps Filming

articles.description:
TL;DR: Jesse Eisenberg guest-starred on a 2014 episode of Modern Family (playing environmentalist neighbor Asher) because he loved the show… but was so averse to watching himself act that he asked producers to send him a version with all his scenes spliced out.  
On Jesse Tyler Ferguson’s Dinner’s On Me podcast (with Alexander Skarsgård), they laughed over Eisenberg’s general reluctance to view his own work—he’ll breeze into premieres, introduce the movie, vanish for two hours and slip back in—anxiety he’s admitted has even made him skittish since the rough reception to his Lex Luthor in Batman v Superman. These days he’s busy writing/directing/star­ring in Oscar-nominated projects like A Real Pain.
articles.title: Jesse Eisenberg asked for a copy of his Modern Family episode with his scenes cut out
